caption: I thought the Lotto was R100 a month. It's R300. What's a number on your statement that surprised you?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R8 600
p/m wages
Living in Mitchells Plain
slides.body:
Male, 41
Married, three kids (14, 9 and 5)
Job: Refuse truck loader, City of Cape Town
Net wages: R8 600 p/m

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: Two bedroom council flat, water, refuse
slides.body: Five of us, two bedrooms. The boys share, my daughter has the lounge corner.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Shoprite specials, the butcher on Friday, bread every day
slides.body: My wife does the sums at the till before the trolley moves. She is never wrong by more than R20.

slides.title: Black tax
slides.includes: My mother's money in Lusikisiki, sent at the Shoprite till
slides.body: It goes first, on the day I'm paid. Before the groceries, before the taxi.

slides.title: Transport
slides.includes: Taxi to the depot at 4am, kids' school taxi
slides.body: I start before the first taxi is full, so I pay a bit more for the early one.

slides.title: Lotto
slides.includes: Wednesday and Saturday Powerball, scratch cards
slides.body: I'd have said R100. It's R300. I know the odds, I buy it anyway.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Electricity, funeral policy, stokvel, airtime, school stationery
slides.body: Funeral policy is R380 and the stokvel is R300. Those two I never skip.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R8 600. A burst geyser or a taxi strike and I'm borrowing from my brother-in-law again.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I uploaded my statement to Beyond Horizon and it grouped everything into categories.

The Lotto line was the one I didn't want to see.

No bank login needed.
